s1.tx: Before the beginning, before the mountains were raised, or ever the earth and the world were formed, there was God.
s1.pc: Bible-first anchor for the pre-temporal frame. The narration borrows the cadence of Psalm 90:2 to set the Father before the created order, asserting His priority over creation without describing a mechanism. D&C 93:29 confirms an eternal frame for both God and the intelligence of man.

b.text: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.
b.comment: The narration echoes this verse's structure to place God prior to the created order.

r.text: Man was also in the beginning with God. Intelligence, or the light of truth, was not created or made, neither indeed can be.
r.comment: Confirms an eternal frame; offered as witness, not as premise.

s2.tx: And He, the Father of Spirits, conceived of our existence from before the foundation of the world, He knew us.
s2.pc: Container-word anchor. 'Father of spirits' (Hebrews 12:9) is a biblical title every tradition can receive; here it grounds the claim that our existence was His to conceive, joined to the foreknowledge of Ephesians 1:4 and Jeremiah 1:5.

b.text: Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?
b.comment: Supplies the biblical title carried by the span.

b.text: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:
b.comment: 'Before the foundation of the world' frame.

b.text: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.
b.comment: Personal foreknowledge, here generalized to all.

r.text: Now the Lord had shown unto me, Abraham, the intelligences that were organized before the world was; and among all these there were many of the noble and great ones;
r.comment: Confirming witness to a premortal company of spirits.

s2b.tx: And so he moved to create us, to fellowship with Him and with one another.
s2b.pc: The purpose behind the creating: not existence only, but communion. The claim gathers from many witnesses rather than one—fellowship with Him (1 Corinthians 1:9; 1 John 1:3; the Lord walking in Eden) and fellowship with one another (Genesis 2:18; John 17; Zion's 'one heart and one mind'), the two great commandments of Matthew 22 binding the two together. Restoration scriptures add the creating's own stated purpose (Moses 1:39; 2 Nephi 2:25) and the communion's promised end (Revelation 21; Moses 7:64). Offered as a cumulative case, welcoming each tradition to fill it from its own scriptures.

b.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
b.comment: Made by divine counsel, in God's image—relational from the first word.

b.text: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
b.comment: The image, and 'male and female'—humanity made for relationship.

b.text: And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.
b.comment: The Lord walking in the garden—the original communion creation was made for.

b.text: And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
b.comment: Eternal life defined as knowing God—fellowship as the end itself.

b.text: God is faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.
b.comment: The explicit vertical purpose: called unto the fellowship of His Son.

b.text: That which we have seen and heard declare we unto you, that ye also may have fellowship with us: and truly our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ.
b.comment: Both directions in one verse: fellowship with the Father and Son, and with one another.

b.text: And I will set my tabernacle among you: and my soul shall not abhor you. And I will walk among you, and will be your God, and ye shall be my people.
b.comment: God's covenant aim: to dwell and walk among His people.

b.text: And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them.
b.comment: The sanctuary built that God may dwell among them.

b.text: And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
b.comment: Not made for isolation—'It is not good that the man should be alone.'

b.text: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.
b.comment: Union with one another patterned on the union of Father and Son.

b.text: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God … In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.
b.comment: No longer strangers, but one household built into a dwelling for God.

b.text: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
b.comment: The two loves that hold both directions together—God, and neighbor.

b.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
b.comment: The Shema—the Old Testament root of the first commandment.

b.text: Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the LORD.
b.comment: The Old Testament root of the second commandment.

b.text: And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.
b.comment: The communion consummated: the tabernacle of God with men.

b.text: And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads.
b.comment: The end of the story: His servants shall see His face.

r.text: For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.
r.comment: The creating's own stated purpose—God's work and glory in His children.

r.text: Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
r.comment: Creation ordered toward joy—men are, that they might have joy.

r.text: In the image of his own body, male and female, created he them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created and became living souls in the land upon the footstool of God.
r.comment: Made in the image of His own body, male and female—embodied relationship.

r.text: Verily, thus saith the Lord: It shall come to pass that every soul who forsaketh his sins and cometh unto me, and calleth on my name, and obeyeth my voice, and keepeth my commandments, shall see my face and know that I am;
r.comment: The promise of the vertical fellowship: to see His face and know Him.

r.text: And that same sociality which exists among us here will exist among us there, only it will be coupled with eternal glory, which glory we do not now enjoy.
r.comment: Fellowship is not left behind—the same sociality, coupled with glory.

r.text: And the Lord called his people Zion, because they were of one heart and one mind, and dwelt in righteousness; and there was no poor among them.
r.comment: Zion named for its fellowship: of one heart and one mind.

r.text: I say unto you, be one; and if ye are not one ye are not mine.
r.comment: The command that makes fellowship the mark of belonging: be one.

r.text: …are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort.
r.comment: Fellowship enacted: to bear one another’s burdens and mourn with those that mourn.

r.text: Wherefore, I give unto them a commandment, saying thus: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, with all thy might, mind, and strength; and in the name of Jesus Christ thou shalt serve him. Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
r.comment: The two loves in Restoration voice: love God, and love thy neighbor.

r.text: And there shall be mine abode, and it shall be Zion, which shall come forth out of all the creations which I have made; and for the space of a thousand years the earth shall rest.
r.comment: The promised end: His abode with His people, called Zion.

s3.tx: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
s3.pc: Direct quotation of John 1:1, the film's Christological hinge. D&C 93:8 is set beside it as a Restoration restatement, confirming rather than extending the Johannine claim.

b.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
b.comment: Quoted verbatim in the narration.

r.text: Therefore, in the beginning the Word was, for he was the Word, even the messenger of salvation—
r.comment: Restoration restatement of the Johannine 'Word.'

s4.tx: The same was in the beginning with God.
s4.pc: Direct quotation of John 1:2, holding the Word with God before the creative acts begin. 3 Nephi 9:15 sets the risen Christ's own testimony beside it—that He was 'with the Father from the beginning'—as a Restoration witness that the Word of the prologue and the Savior are one, confirming the Johannine claim rather than arguing it.

b.text: The same was in the beginning with God.
b.comment: Quoted verbatim in the narration.

r.text: Behold, I am Jesus Christ the Son of God. I created the heavens and the earth, and all things that in them are. I was with the Father from the beginning. I am in the Father, and the Father in me; and in me hath the Father glorified his name.
r.comment: The risen Christ names Himself Creator and 'with the Father from the beginning'; offered as convergent witness, not premise.

s5.tx: All things were made by Him, and without Him was not anything made that was made.
s5.pc: Direct quotation of John 1:3, with Colossians 1:16 widening the scope of the Word's creative agency. Moses 1:32 confirms the same agency in Restoration language.

b.text: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.
b.comment: Quoted verbatim in the narration.

b.text: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:
b.comment: Widens the scope of the Word's creative agency.

r.text: And by the word of my power, have I created them, which is mine Only Begotten Son, who is full of grace and truth.
r.comment: Creation by the word, through the Son.

s6.tx: In the Word was life, and that life was the light of men.
s6.pc: Near-verbatim John 1:4; the narration substitutes 'the Word' for the pronoun to keep the referent plain. Doctrine and Covenants 93:9 echoes the same pairing of life and light in Restoration language—'in him was the life of men and the light of men'—a restatement, not an addition.

b.text: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.
b.comment: The verse the narration renders, with 'the Word' supplied for the pronoun.

r.text: The light and the Redeemer of the world; the Spirit of truth, who came into the world, because the world was made by him, and in him was the life of men and the light of men.
r.comment: Restoration restatement pairing life and light in the Word.

s7.tx: His light shineth in darkness, and the darkness comprehended it not.
s7.pc: Near-verbatim John 1:5. Doctrine and Covenants 88:49 restates it almost word for word and turns it toward promise—'the day shall come when you shall comprehend even God'—confirming the image while extending its hope.

b.text: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
b.comment: Quoted, lightly adapted ('His light').

r.text: The light shineth in darkness, and the darkness comprehendeth it not; nevertheless, the day shall come when you shall comprehend even God, being quickened in him and by him.
r.comment: Near-verbatim restatement, carried toward the eventual comprehension of God.

s8.tx: The Word of God spoke the heavens and the earth into being.
s8.pc: A compression of the whole 'He spake, and it was done' witness. Psalm 33:6 and 33:9 supply the biblical ground—the heavens made by the word, done at His speaking—with Hebrews 11:3 naming the worlds framed by God's word and 2 Peter 3:5 recalling that by that word the heavens were of old. Jacob 4:9 is the Restoration's own creation-by-word verse, confirming that what the Word spoke, was.

b.text: By the word of the LORD were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.
b.comment: The heavens made by the word of the LORD.

b.text: For he spake, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood fast.
b.comment: 'He spake, and it was done'—the creative word enacted.

b.text: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.
b.comment: The worlds framed by the word of God.

b.text: For this they willingly are ignorant of, that by the word of God the heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and in the water:
b.comment: By the word of God the heavens were of old.

r.text: For behold, by the power of his word man came upon the face of the earth, which earth was created by the power of his word.
r.comment: Creation by the power of His word, in Restoration voice.

s9.tx: [ ♫ music ♫ ] But the earth was without form and void.
s9.pc: Genesis 1:2, first clause. Moses 2:2 gives the same in first-person Restoration voice, and Abraham 4:2 in the language of the Gods ('empty and desolate'); the three accounts converge on one scene. Genesis 1:2 carries s9 through s11, each span rendering one clause of the single verse.

b.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
b.comment: 'Without form, and void'—the opening condition of the earth.

r.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and I caused darkness to come up upon the face of the deep; and my Spirit moved upon the face of the water; for I am God.
r.comment: First-person Restoration parallel.

r.text: And the earth, after it was formed, was empty and desolate, because they had not formed anything but the earth; and darkness reigned upon the face of the deep, and the Spirit of the Gods was brooding upon the face of the waters.
r.comment: The account of the Gods: 'empty and desolate.'

s10.tx: Darkness was upon the face of the deep.
s10.pc: Genesis 1:2, second clause—darkness over the deep. Moses 2:2 and Abraham 4:2 stand as the same Restoration witnesses; the anchor is the one verse's next clause, not a new event.

b.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
b.comment: 'Darkness was upon the face of the deep.'

r.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and I caused darkness to come up upon the face of the deep; and my Spirit moved upon the face of the water; for I am God.
r.comment: Restoration parallel (darkness over the deep).

r.text: And the earth, after it was formed, was empty and desolate, because they had not formed anything but the earth; and darkness reigned upon the face of the deep, and the Spirit of the Gods was brooding upon the face of the waters.
r.comment: 'Darkness reigned upon the face of the deep.'

s11.tx: [ ♫ music ♫ ] The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
s11.pc: Genesis 1:2, final clause—the Spirit upon the waters. Moses 2:2 renders it 'my Spirit moved upon the face of the water'; Abraham 4:2 'brooding upon the face of the waters'—the Restoration accounts vary the image without altering the scene.

b.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
b.comment: 'The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.'

r.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and I caused darkness to come up upon the face of the deep; and my Spirit moved upon the face of the water; for I am God.
r.comment: 'My Spirit moved upon the face of the water.'

r.text: And the earth, after it was formed, was empty and desolate, because they had not formed anything but the earth; and darkness reigned upon the face of the deep, and the Spirit of the Gods was brooding upon the face of the waters.
r.comment: 'Brooding upon the face of the waters.'

s12.pc: Genesis 1:3, the first creative command. Moses 2:3 and Abraham 4:3 confirm the identical command—'Let there be light; and there was light'—across the three accounts.

b.text: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
b.comment: The first spoken command of creation.

r.text: And I, God, said: Let there be light; and there was light.
r.comment: Restoration parallel, first person.

r.text: And they (the Gods) said: Let there be light; and there was light.
r.comment: The Gods speak the same command.

s13.tx: And He divided the light from the darkness, saying, “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters to divide the waters from the waters.” And God called the firmament heaven.
s13.pc: Three Genesis verses compressed into one beat: the dividing of light from darkness (1:4), the firmament in the midst of the waters (1:6), and its naming as Heaven (1:8). Moses 2:6-8 tracks the same acts in first-person voice; Abraham 4:6-8 renders the firmament as an 'expanse' the Gods order until obeyed.

b.text: And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
b.comment: God divides the light from the darkness.

b.text: And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.
b.comment: The firmament in the midst of the waters.

b.text: And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.
b.comment: The firmament called Heaven; the second day.

r.text: And again, I, God, said: Let there be a firmament in the midst of the water, and it was so, even as I spake; and I said: Let it divide the waters from the waters; and it was done;
r.comment: Restoration parallel: the firmament, first person.

r.text: And I, God, called the firmament Heaven; and the evening and the morning were the second day.
r.comment: 'I, God, called the firmament Heaven.'

r.text: And the Gods also said: Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and it shall divide the waters from the waters.
r.comment: Abraham's account: an 'expanse' in the midst of the waters.

r.text: And the Gods called the expanse, Heaven. And it came to pass that it was from evening until morning that they called night; and it came to pass that it was from morning until evening that they called day; and this was the second time that they called night and day.
r.comment: The Gods name the expanse Heaven.

s14.tx: [ ♫ music ♫ ] God spoke again, “Let the waters be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear.”
s14.pc: Genesis 1:9—the waters gathered, dry land appearing. Moses 2:9 and Abraham 4:9 give the Restoration parallels; Abraham's 'and it was so as they ordered' carries that account's distinctive obedience refrain.

b.text: And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.
b.comment: The waters gathered; the dry land appears.

r.text: And I, God, said: Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and it was so; and I, God, said: Let there be dry land; and it was so.
r.comment: First-person Restoration parallel.

r.text: And the Gods ordered, saying: Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the earth come up dry; and it was so as they ordered;
r.comment: The Gods order; 'it was so as they ordered.'

s15.tx: And God called the dry land earth.
s15.pc: Genesis 1:10, first clause—the naming of the dry land Earth. Moses 2:10 and Abraham 4:10 confirm; Genesis 1:10 carries both s15 and s16, split at its two naming-clauses.

b.text: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.
b.comment: 'God called the dry land Earth.'

r.text: And I, God, called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, called I the Sea; and I, God, saw that all things which I had made were good.
r.comment: First-person Restoration parallel.

r.text: And the Gods pronounced the dry land, Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, pronounced they, Great Waters; and the Gods saw that they were obeyed.
r.comment: The Gods 'pronounced' the land and waters.

s16.tx: The gathering together of the waters called He seas.
s16.pc: Genesis 1:10, second clause—the gathered waters called Seas. The same Moses 2:10 and Abraham 4:10 witnesses stand; the anchor is the verse's next naming-clause, not a new act.

b.text: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.
b.comment: 'The gathering together of the waters called he Seas.'

r.text: And I, God, called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, called I the Sea; and I, God, saw that all things which I had made were good.
r.comment: Restoration parallel (the seas).

r.text: And the Gods pronounced the dry land, Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, pronounced they, Great Waters; and the Gods saw that they were obeyed.
r.comment: The Gods pronounce the waters 'Great Waters.'

s17.tx: God, the Father of Spirits, gathered a Divine Council of heavenly beings.
s17.pc: Scripture repeatedly shows God amid a heavenly council. The host stands by His throne (1 Kings 22:19); the sons of God present themselves before Him (Job 1:6); the assembly of the holy ones surrounds Him (Psalm 89). Restoration scripture names it: the Council of the Eternal God before this world was (Doctrine and Covenants 121:32), the noble and great ones organized before the world (Abraham 3:22–23), the seraphic hosts of heaven before the world was made (Doctrine and Covenants 38:1). 'Father of Spirits' carries from Hebrews 12:9.

b.text: And he said, Hear thou therefore the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.
b.comment: The LORD enthroned amid all the host of heaven — the council seen.

b.text: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD…
b.comment: The sons of God presenting themselves before the LORD — the heavenly court assembled.

b.text: God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.
b.comment: God presiding in the divine assembly.

b.text: And the heavens shall praise thy wonders, O LORD: thy faithfulness also in the congregation of the saints… God is greatly to be feared in the assembly of the saints, and to be had in reverence of all them that are about him.
b.comment: The assembly of the holy ones gathered about the LORD.

b.text: For who hath stood in the counsel of the LORD, and hath perceived and heard his word? who hath marked his word, and heard it?
b.comment: The prophetic 'counsel of the LORD' — the divine deliberative assembly.

b.text: A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
b.comment: Ten thousand times ten thousand of the heavenly host standing before Him.

r.text: Now the Lord had shown unto me, Abraham, the intelligences that were organized before the world was; and among all these there were many of the noble and great ones; And God saw these souls that they were good, and he stood in the midst of them, and he said: These I will make my rulers; for he stood among those that were spirits, and he saw that they were good; and he said unto me: Abraham, thou art one of them; thou wast chosen before thou wast born.
r.comment: The noble and great ones organized before the world; God stood in the midst of the assembly.

r.text: According to that which was ordained in the midst of the Council of the Eternal God of all other gods before this world was, that should be reserved unto the finishing and the end thereof, when every man shall enter into his eternal presence and into his immortal rest.
r.comment: Named plainly: the Council of the Eternal God, before this world was.

r.text: Thus saith the Lord your God, even Jesus Christ, the Great I Am, Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the same which looked upon the wide expanse of eternity, and all the seraphic hosts of heaven, before the world was made;
r.comment: Christ beheld all the seraphic hosts of heaven before the world was made.

s19.tx: “When I laid the foundations of the earth.
s19.pc: The Lord answers Job out of the whirlwind by pointing back to the founding of the earth — a work the heavenly host witnessed and no mortal saw (Job 38:4). The same laying of the earth's foundations is sung across the Psalms and the Prophets.

b.text: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
b.comment: The Lord's question to Job — the words the narration renders.

b.text: Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever.
b.comment: The LORD who laid the earth's foundations.

b.text: When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth:
b.comment: Present when He appointed the foundations of the earth.

b.text: Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heavens: when I call unto them, they stand up together.
b.comment: The LORD's own hand laid the earth's foundation.

s20.tx: The morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy.”
s20.pc: Job 38:7, quoted almost word for word — the heavenly host rejoicing as the earth was founded. Joseph Smith takes up the same words as praise (Doctrine and Covenants 128:23), calling the morning stars and the sons of God to sing and shout again.

b.text: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
b.comment: The verse the narration renders — the hosts rejoicing at the founding.

r.text: …And let the sun, moon, and the morning stars sing together, and let all the sons of God shout for joy! And let the eternal creations declare his name forever and ever!
r.comment: Joseph Smith takes up Job's words as praise — the morning stars and sons of God called to sing and shout again.

s21.tx: The first among them was the WORD, the First Born of every creature, the express image of the Father.
s21.pc: Among the council, one is preeminent — the Word (John 1:1). Scripture names Him the firstborn of every creature and the image of the invisible God (Colossians 1:15), the express image of the Father's person (Hebrews 1:3), and the bright and morning star (Revelation 22:16) — first among the morning stars just heard singing. Restoration scripture calls Him plainly the Firstborn (Doctrine and Covenants 93:21) and shows Him standing in the council as the one like unto God who led the creation (Abraham 3:24).

b.text: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:
b.comment: Both titles in one verse: the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.

b.text: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
b.comment: 'The express image of his person' — the phrase the narration renders.

b.text: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.
b.comment: Christ the bright and morning star — first among the morning stars just heard.

r.text: And now, verily I say unto you, I was in the beginning with the Father, and am the Firstborn;
r.comment: Christ's own words: 'I was in the beginning with the Father, and am the Firstborn.'

r.text: And there stood one among them that was like unto God, and he said unto those who were with him: We will go down, for there is space there, and we will take of these materials, and we will make an earth whereon these may dwell;
r.comment: The one 'like unto God' standing preeminent in the council, who led the creation.

s22.tx: This same Word would be born as Jesus of Nazareth.

s23.tx: The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us.

s24.tx: He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not.

s25.tx: Of the Father are all things.

s26.tx: And by the Son in heaven and in earth, visible and invisible, all things were created by Him, and for Him, and by Him all things consist.

s27.tx: He is before all things the Heir of all things, by whom God the Father made the worlds.

s28.tx: The Word commanded, “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide day from night.

s29.tx: Let them be for signs and for seasons, for days and for years.”

s30.tx: Two lights were made to shine.

s31.tx: The greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night.

s33.tx: God did not create the earth in vain.

s34.tx: He formed it to be inhabited.

s36.tx: “Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life: great whales, and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought forth abundantly.”

s37.tx: “Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the tree yielding fruit.” And God blessed them all, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas.”

s38.tx: “Let the earth bring forth living creatures, the cattle, and creeping things, and beasts of the earth, and fowl that may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.

s39.tx: Let them multiply upon the earth.”

s40.tx: Then God the Father said to the Divine council, “Let us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, male and female.”

s41.tx: He formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into him the breath of life.

s42.tx: And man became a living soul.

s43.tx: And God planted a garden eastward in Eden.

s44.tx: And there he put the man whom he had formed to dress it and to keep it.

s45.tx: The father said, “It is not good that the man should be alone.”

s46.tx: So He made a woman and brought her unto the man, explaining, “Therefore shall a man cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh.”

s47.tx: And God commanded, “Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing upon the earth.” God blessed them, and said unto them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it, and have dominion over all life.”

s48.tx: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them. And God looked upon everything that He had made.

s49.tx: And behold, it was very good.

s50.tx: The invisible God could be known through the visible creation.

s51.tx: Then God rested from all his work which He created and made.

s52.tx: God knew beforehand that Eden would not last, that humankind would be deceived, tempted, sin, and fall from the presence of God to mortality.

s53.tx: Still, the father had chosen us in him before the foundation of the world.

s54.tx: The dramatic events that took place in the garden led to the conditions of mortality and opposition in all things.

s55.tx: It was by God's plan that creation and the state of humankind was brought to their present state.

s58.tx: “Behold, mankind has become as one of us to know good and evil.”

s59.tx: Then the Father asked, “Who shall I send?

s60.tx: Who among you is willing to maintain the holy demands of justice while offering atoning mercy and divine grace?”

s61.tx: The Word saw that there was no one, and marveled that there was no intercessor.

s62.tx: So by His own arm mankind must be saved.

s63.tx: He volunteered to be the Lamb, slain from the foundation of the world.

s64.tx: He was for ordained and anointed by God the Father before the foundation of the world, to be the Messiah who would show mankind the way and redeem souls unto the Father.

s65.tx: The Word who created heaven and earth, Jehovah of the Old Testament, was the same God that would be born as Jesus of Nazareth, the Savior and Redeemer of the world.

s66.tx: Before withdrawing His presence from the children He had created, God made coats of skins of animals to clothe them.

s67.tx: He gave them instructions and sent them forth from Eden to till the ground from whence mankind was taken.

s68.tx: The Word came to Adam, “In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground.

s69.tx: For out of it was thou taken.

s70.tx: For dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.”

s71.tx: Most important of all these events, God promised eventual victory over evil and the fall of mankind.

s72.tx: Adam was comforted by the promise of eternal life God made from before the world began, knowing God cannot lie.

s73.tx: By Divine Will we experience desire, hardship, sorrow, temptations, enmity, labor, and death.

s74.tx: But this is not all we were also meant to know fulfillment, comfort, joy, holy inspiration, love, rest, and life. For each of these life experiences carries its opposite that we might know the one by the other.

s75.tx: Adam taught his posterity of God's promises of salvation from evil, and redemption from the fall from God's presence.

s76.tx: From that time, men began to call upon the name of the Lord.

s77.tx: Their faith and hope were expressed through prayer, worship, and through sacrifices that foreshadowed the atoning sacrifice of the promised Messiah.

s78.tx: The Great Patriarchs and Prophets knew these things since the world began.

s79.tx: Each of them learning to walk with God.

s80.tx: For the Spirit of Christ, which was in them, testified before hand of the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow those that do His commandments.

s81.tx: For they will have the right to the Tree of Life restored to them as they enter through the gates into the Kingdom of Heaven.

s83.tx: We lift our eyes to the work of your fingers.

s84.tx: The moon and the stars you set in their places.

s85.tx: And the heavens declare your glory.

s86.tx: The skies proclaim the work of your hands.

s87.tx: Day after day they shout their witness.

s88.tx: Night after night they reveal knowledge.

s91.tx: Their voice still carries to the ends of the earth.

s92.tx: And so we come before You and wonder...

s93.tx: Through your Beloved Son, You made all this, and us.

s94.tx: You are the Divine Shepherd of the starry host, calling each of them by name and by Your great power, Not one of them is missing.

s95.tx: By Your word the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of Your mouth.

s96.tx: When You laid the foundations, the Morning Stars sang together, and the Children of God shouted for joy.

s97.tx: All things bear witness of You. The earth and everything upon it.

s98.tx: Its motion and the planets moving in their fixed courses.

s99.tx: The earth turns upon her wings.

s100.tx: The sun gives light by day, the moon by night.

s101.tx: And the stars shine as they move in their glory.

s102.tx: And in even the least of these, we have seen You moving in majesty and power.

s103.tx: We thank You that nothing You have made is without its witness.

s104.tx: The animals teach us of You.

s105.tx: The birds of the sky tell of You.

s106.tx: The earth instructs us, and the fish of the sea declare the work of Your hand.

s107.tx: For which of them does not know that Your hand has done this?

s108.tx: All things You have made bear witness of You.

s109.tx: Things in the heavens above, things upon the earth, things beneath. All of them testify of You.

s110.tx: Everything You have given points to You.

s111.tx: And in the fullness of it all we behold Your Son, through whom all things were made.

s112.tx: He came to us as an offering, a sacrifice to save and redeem the world.

s113.tx: And into all this vastness, You still turn Your face toward us.

s114.tx: What are we that You keep us in mind?

s115.tx: What are mortal children that You care for us?

s116.tx: Yet You have made us a little lower than the angels, and crowned us with glory and honor.

s117.tx: You have given us charge over the works of Your hands and entrusted the earth to our care.

s118.tx: You created us in Your own image and called us Your own.

s119.tx: For this we have no worthy words, only thanks.

s121.tx: Oh, Father, let us never fail to see it.

s122.tx: Since the world was made, Your unseen qualities, Your eternal power, Your very nature have been plain in the things You have made.

s123.tx: And we will not turn our eyes away.

s124.tx: So we confess Your hand in all things, and withhold nothing from Your will.

s125.tx: All creation answers You, and we answer with it.

s126.tx: Let the sun and moon praise You.

s127.tx: Let all the shining stars praise You.

s129.tx: For at Your command they were created.

s130.tx: The hills break forth and singing before You.

s131.tx: And all the trees of the field clap their hands for joy.

s132.tx: God our Father, how majestic is Your name in all the earth.

s133.tx: Send us from this place with eyes open to Your glory, hearts humbled by Your goodness, and hands willing to care for all You have made.

s134.tx: We offer this prayer in the name of Your Son, Jesus Christ.
